title: Quick check: JavaScript Functions

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “JavaScript Functions”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Function declarations should be demonstrated with a small example while preserving predictable data transformations.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Function declarations should be demonstrated with a small example while preserving predictable data transformations.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in JavaScript Functions: Function declarations should be demonstrated with a small example while preserving predictable data transformations.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Function declarations?
options: Prefer clear functions, explicit modules, and immutable data transformations.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Prefer clear functions, explicit modules, and immutable data transformations.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in JavaScript Functions: Prefer clear functions, explicit modules, and immutable data transformations.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “JavaScript Functions” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in JavaScript Functions: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
